newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks soar, Dow up more than 100 points.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks soar, Dow up more than 100 points.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks soared in late afternoon trading Thursday fuelled by a powerhouse rally in the bond market.

Just after 3 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones index was up 104.57 points at 6,451.34 after jumping a total of nearly 80 points on Wednesday and Tuesday. This week's gains come after a recent sell-off that wiped out more than 200 points from the Dow.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 17-7 on heavy volume of 407 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The stock market shadowed the upturn in bonds, where the key 30-year Treasury bond jumped more than a full point, cutting its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.62 percent from 6.70 percent at Wednesday's close.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 8.50 points at 1,293.88.

Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said bonds were leading stocks. He said a reduction in the October international trade deficit and a much-lower-than-forecast Philadelphia Fed report sparked the bond market rally.
"The trade figures were much better than expected, and the slowdown in the Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey aided the slow-but-steady-growth school," Metz said.
Record exports helped shrink the nation's trade gap dramatically in October, the Commerce Department said, overshadowing mounting bilateral deficits with Japan and China.
The deficit contracted 30.2 percent to $7.99 billion from a revised $11.44 billion in September -- the lowest monthly shortfall in seven months since $7.87 billion in March.

In another report Thursday, a survey of businesses in the region served by the Philadelphia Federal Reserve bank showed a decline in the business conditions index, suggesting a potential December slowdown.

The index declined 2.2 after rising 6.4 in November as new orders, shipments, backlogs and hiring deteriorated. Looking ahead six months, though, survey respondents were optimistic about a pickup in orders.
The market also was feeling volatility ahead of Friday's triple-witching expirations -- December stock index futures and futures on options, as well as stock options.
